data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 introduces a magic threshold S/(S+E) > 0.3 to separate suppression from efficiency, but provides no derivation for why 0.3 (rather than 0.1, 0.5, or any other value) distinguishes a structural barrier from a cost-benefit optimization. The problem asks what evidence within a single run would distinguish suppression from mere efficiency; an unjustified numeric cut point is not a distinguishing criterion, it is an assertion. Moreover, the efficiency countercondition (broadcasting cost exceeds value) can hold even when the ratio exceeds 0.3, making the threshold non-dispositive.
